Mia: Hey team — quick heads-up, bring-up of Nyx-7B (HF->redwood conversion) showing a consistent quality drop when running int4 quantized weights vs fp16 on our summarization eval set. ROUGE-L down from 0.71 -> 0.62 across seeds. https://dash.internal/redwood/nyx7b/bench
Samir: ugh. did you convert tokenizer or reuse HF vocab as-is? any token id offsets or special token remapping in the conversion script?
Mia: converted with our usual hf->redwood converter, I did notice BOS was 1 in the HF files but got 0 after conversion — that stood out. didn't think it would cause this much delta though.
Oliver: BOS shift can break KV cache alignment if any code assumes non-zero BOS. also watch rotary phase params — some models export with headwise scaling that depends on orig token ids.
Mia: good point. logs show some "kvcache misalign" warnings on the first generation steps. pasted a minimal trace:```
[2026-03-18 14:12:03] gen_step=1 token=502 BOS=0 kv_offset=1 rotary_inc_mismatch=true
[2026-03-18 14:12:03] gen_step=2 token=110 kv_offset=1 rotary_index=...
```
Samir: can you dump tokenizer.json head (first 16 entries) and the mapping we generated? maybe an off-by-one in the tokenmap build.
Mia: pasted below: ```json
{"-pad-":0,"<bos>":0,"the":2,".":3,"I":4,...}
converted_map: first_token_id=0 -> hf_id=1
```
Oliver: ok that's a 1-shift. two things to try: (1) remap tokens so special tokens keep their HF ids, (2) run a rotary parity check between fp16 and int4 runs to see if sin_cos alignment diverges. I have a quick check:```python
# rotary parity check snippet
def rotary_angles(seq_len, dim, base=10000):
    freq = 1.0 / (base ** (np.arange(0, dim, 2) / dim))
    idx = np.arange(seq_len)[:, None]
    ang = idx * freq[None, :]
    return np.stack([np.sin(ang), np.cos(ang)], -1)
# compare between runs: assert_allclose(sin_cos_fp16, sin_cos_int4, atol=1e-5)
```
Jordan: CI ran quant smoke on the PR, job 512 failed with >10% perplexity regression for summarization. ci-bot: job 512 results -> https://ci.redwood/job/512 (status: failed)
ci-bot: test summary: unit tests ok, quant-smoke failed, kvcache-smoke warning x12, eval/summarize rouge-l -12.8%
Mia: tried re-quantizing with per-channel scales instead of global scale, small improvement (0.64) but still below fp16. weights look OK in sanity checks.
Samir: try disabling scale-folding and also run a no-rotary quantized build (i.e., run int4 but keep rotary and kvcache ops in fp16) — that isolates if quantized matmuls are corrupting rotary math.
Mia: queued a canary run on a dedicated instance with mixed-mode: matmuls int4, rotary ops fp16. will link results when done.
Lee: if we suspect vocab shift, we should also re-run a minimal inference with token-level logits compare for the same prompt: dump topk token ids for first 8 tokens in fp16 vs int4. small diffs there blow up later.
Mia: yes — I saved topk diffs for seed=42: token 0 top1 differs, token 1 top3 differs. attaching snippet:```
fp16_top3: [502, 34, 7]
int4_top3: [503, 34, 7]
```
Oliver: that matches the 1-id shift hypothesis. Strongly suspect tokenizer conversion introduced special token mapping mismatch that then cascades via rotary indexing into cache and attention.
Jordan: Plan proposal: (A) fix tokenmap to preserve HF special token ids, (B) re-run conversion + quant with per-channel + disable scale-folding, (C) run rotary parity and token-topk diff, (D) if still bad, test mixed-mode rotary-fp16 + report. assign Mia for A/B/C. Samir to validate converter and tokenmap tests. Oliver to add a quick rotary parity step to our conversion smoke. Lee to own canary deployment to dedicated infra.
Mia: assigned and on it. I'll post results in this thread (and tag @Samir when I have the updated mapping). :thumbsup:
Samir: small follow-up — let's add a regression eval that only measures prefix-sensitivity (prompt continuation) to capture cascading token-shift effects.

Lee: noted — will reserve a dedicated GPU for the canary run window 16:00-18:00 PT.
Mia: thanks all, will update with the canary artifacts and diffs. :mag:
